doc.title: Horn Shirley — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Staying home, image and being a woman leader
title: Refusing to be a stand-up singer for Mercury
summary: Mercury wanted to cultivate her as a standing girl singer; she insisted on sitting at the piano.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Okay. Then he had Cannonball. He had the top acts, and at the end of that top- act business was me, and he cared about me. Okay? He knew in the beginning that I was not ready to go . . . I didn‘t want to be in show business. I just wanted to be one of the guys. I want to play the music. I want . . . and, he‘s my friend right today, and he cares about me. If Mercury wanted me to stand up and be a stand-up singer, I don‘t want no stand-up singer. I‘m going to play the piano. That‘s my forte, right. Hence I didn‘t stand up to sing, and I mean, John never tried to push me, you know, because he knew what I wanted to do. So there was not any problem, you know. I wasn‘t going to be a . . . do you remember Mercury? Dinah Washington was the hottest thing in the world, right. Okay. Nancy wanted to step in there, but Nancy wasn‘t strong enough to step in there with Dinah.

Okay, so that went along, right? Meanwhile, they were trying to ease me in to have another feel for Mercury, and I wasn‘t into that, and I said no. I said, ―John, I don‘t want to do it. I‘m going to sit down and play for myself. I‘m not going to stand up.‖
So Mercury really was trying to cultivate another girl singer.
Strictly a girl singer, not a musician.

Trying to cultivate me, and Quincy was in there trying to push it, and I said no. But no, that wasn‘t my thing. I wasn‘t interested, and I thank God, you know. I have been lucky that people . . . John Levy loves me today, like I love him, and he respects me, and Quincy, too, you know. They know that I‘m not into that other stuff. I‘m not there. They respect me for what I feel, and I‘m a musician, and that‘s that. I can‘t be anything else but, you know, and that‘s it.
